title: Medication Reconciliation at Admission and Discharge
subject: Prescription Pearls
preview: Medication reconciliation compares the patient's actual medicines against admission, transfer or discharge orders.
quickRevision: Medication reconciliation compares the patient's actual medicines against admission, transfer or discharge orders.
Discrepancies include omissions, duplications, wrong frequencies and unintended continuation of temporary therapies.
Explain changes in plain language and communicate a current medication list to the next care setting.

sections.title: Recognize the situation
points: Medication reconciliation compares the patient's actual medicines against admission, transfer or discharge orders.
Include prescription medicines, OTC agents, supplements, allergies, doses and recent changes.

sections.title: Clinical decisions & differential
points: Discrepancies include omissions, duplications, wrong frequencies and unintended continuation of temporary therapies.
Explain changes in plain language and communicate a current medication list to the next care setting.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: A recorded drug list is not necessarily an accurate history until verified with reliable sources.

quiz.question: What is medication reconciliation intended to detect?
quiz.explanation: Unintended medication discrepancies. Discrepancies include omissions, duplications, wrong frequencies and unintended continuation of temporary therapies.
